In this trial, radiotherapy was administered during ICI maintenance after chemoimmunotherapy. Platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy achieves maximal tumor response in the induction phase but carries substantial toxicity. Based on the “in situ tumor vaccine” concept, SABR plus ICI has been widely explored in advanced solid tumors. Although the clinical benefit of ISABR has been suggested in NSCLC, the reported outcomes show considerable heterogeneity across studies 10, 41, 42. This heterogeneity is largely driven by inter- and intratumoral genomic diversity, which generates distinct immune microenvironments in primary and metastatic sites 43, 44, limiting systemic immune activation and consistent abscopal effects 45. To address this problem, some clinicians have proposed irradiating multiple lesions rather than relying on single-site SABR 46. However, that approach is often limited by technical challenges, including the inability to deliver ablative doses to large tumors and to tumors that are located close to critical structures 47. The local efficacy of SABR in this trial may also reflect the intrinsic potency of ablative doses rather than immune effects alone. Accordingly, LDRT has emerged as a practical complementary strategy to remodel the TIME 20, 48, 49, enhance immune cell infiltration, and potentiate antitumor immunity 48, 50.
